**“Describe the mechanism of normal vaginal delivery.”**

“In a normal vertex occipito-anterior delivery, the mechanism consists of engagement, descent, flexion, internal rotation, extension, restitution, external rotation and expulsion. Engagement occurs when the biparietal diameter passes through the pelvic inlet. As descent occurs, flexion brings the chin towards the chest and presents the smaller suboccipitobregmatic diameter. The occiput then rotates to align appropriately with the maternal pelvis. Once the head reaches the pelvic outlet, it extends and delivers beneath the pubic arch. After delivery of the head, restitution occurs as the head realigns with the shoulders, followed by external rotation as the shoulders rotate internally. The anterior shoulder, posterior shoulder and remainder of the body then deliver.”
